articles.title: PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF) highlighted as a cheap big-cap stock with low PE
articles.body: The article focuses on PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF), the Grup Salim issuer controlled by Anthoni Salim, being a low-priced big-cap stock. It notes that INDF trades at a trailing-twelve-month price-to-earnings ratio of 6.19× and closed at Rp 6,750, down 2.8% on 25 Sept 2026, with a weekly decline of 3.9% and a month-to-date drop of 8.4% while YTD it is only 0.3% lower. Financially, INDF posted Q2‑2026 revenue of Rp 31.6 trillion (‑6.7% QoQ, +11.8% YoY) and cumulative H1‑2026 revenue of Rp 65.5 trillion (+9.5% YoY); core profit fell 8.5% QoQ to Rp 3.1 trillion but rose 26% YoY, leading to H1 core profit of Rp 6.4 trillion (+6.9% YoY). Net profit declined 33.1% YoY to Rp 4.7 trillion, driven by a foreign‑exchange loss of Rp 3.4 trillion versus Rp 231 million a year earlier.

articles.title: Foreign investors' net selling makes ten stocks, including PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI), top losers as the IHSG falls
articles.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp559 billion on Friday, 25 September 2026, making ten stocks the largest foreign outflow victims while the IHSG weakened by 56.7 points (0.9%) to 6,241.8 at market close. Net sell in the regular market amounted to Rp440.3 billion and Rp118.7 billion in the negotiation and cash markets, with total transaction value reaching Rp9.3 trillion. The biggest foreign sell-offs were PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) with Rp62.8 billion, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) with Rp37.8 billion, PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) with Rp29.2 billion, TLKM with Rp112.7 billion and PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk with Rp71 billion. Overall, 122 stocks rose, 587 fell and 254 remained unchanged during the session.

articles.title: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) records largest foreign net buy as market sells intensify
articles.body: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA), an issuer owned by Edwin Soeryadjaya and Winato Kartono, recorded the largest foreign net purchase of Rp 76.8 billion during 21‑25 September 2026 while the Indonesian market posted a total foreign net sell of Rp 3.1 trillion. The net buying made MDKA the top‑ranked stock, ahead of PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (TAPG), which attracted a foreign net buy of Rp 70.1 billion and is owned by TP Rachmat LR Imanto and Meity Subianto. In the first half of 2026 MDKA reported a net profit of US$102 million, reversing a US$16 million loss from the same period a year earlier, with consolidated revenue rising 64 % year‑on‑year to US$1.4 billion. EBITDA increased 191 % to US$512 million, driven by stronger nickel and gold operations.

articles.title: Foreign investors dump these stocks over the week as the IDX Composite falls 3.09% to 6,241.89
articles.body: The article reports that foreign investors sold large amounts of shares in ten listed companies during the week when the IDX Composite (IHSG) fell 3.09% to 6,241.89 points. Over the week, foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 4.39 trillion across the market, with a further Rp 559.07 billion sold on Friday alone. The ten most heavily net‑sold stocks were PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) (Rp 149.63 billion), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS) (Rp 82.11 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) (Rp 79.98 billion), PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (TAPG) (Rp 67.23 billion), PT Indokripto Koin Semesta Tbk (COIN) (Rp 48.70 billion), PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk (VKTR) (Rp 44.98 billion), PT Erajaya Swasembada Tbk (ERAA) (Rp 35.61 billion), PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) (Rp 29.44 billion), PT Singaraja Putra Tbk (SINI) (Rp 28.42 billion) and PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk (BREN) (Rp 18.91 billion). These companies, representing large‑cap and sector‑diverse issuers, were the primary targets of the foreign sell‑off, while other large‑cap stocks, including banks, saw mixed activity with some foreign accumulation. The concentration of foreign selling on these ten issuers contributed to the overall downward pressure on the IHSG during the week.

articles.title: United Tractors' long journey toward a sustainable industry
articles.body: United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) is pursuing a transformation to balance its coal and non‑coal businesses to 50:50 by 2030 and cut greenhouse‑gas emissions 30% by that year. The company is optimizing its core through subsidiary PT Pamapersada Nusantara (PAMA), which has adopted ERP S/4HANA and Mine Image Recognition, while diversifying into nickel via subsidiary PT Danusa Tambang Nusantara (DTN) smelter and gold via subsidiary PT Agincourt Resources (PTAR) with biodiversity‑focused ESG due diligence. Renewable‑energy efforts are channeled through subsidiary PT Energi Prima Nusantara (EPN), which holds a 31.49% stake in PT Arkora Hydro Tbk (ARKO) operating 27.4 MW of hydro capacity and 15.4 MW under construction, alongside floating solar projects, geothermal exploration via PT Supreme Energy Rantau Dedap (SERD) and waste‑to‑energy partnerships. Up to 30 June 2026, UNTR reported net revenue of Rp58.28 trillion and net profit of Rp956 billion, with segment revenues of Rp14.97 trillion (heavy equipment), Rp27.16 trillion (mining contractor), Rp12.86 trillion (thermal & metallurgical coal) and Rp2.35 trillion (non‑coal mineral mining); emissions intensity fell to 12.03% in 2025 and renewable‑energy consumption rose to 23.99 million GJ, including 15,298.56 GJ from solar.

articles.title: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) reports US$102 million net profit for H1 2026, reversing US$16 million loss
articles.body: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) posted a net profit attributable to the parent of US$102 million in the first half of 2026, up from a loss of US$16 million in the same period a year earlier. Consolidated revenue rose 64 percent year‑on‑year to US$1.40 billion and EBITDA surged 191 percent to US$512 million. The turnaround was driven by strong performance of its subsidiaries, with PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) remaining the largest contributor to MDKA’s EBITDA through higher nickel ore production (15.2 million wmt, up 121 %) and sales, while PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (EMAS) boosted earnings with a 32 percent increase in gold output to 66,814 ounces. The group also highlighted progress on strategic projects such as the Tujuh Bukit copper feasibility study and expansion of the Pani gold mine, supporting long‑term value creation.

articles.title: Second Liner Stocks Remain Prospective Through End‑2026, Catalysts Highlighted
articles.body: The article discusses that second‑liner equities are still viewed as having upside potential up to the end of 2026, supported by specific catalysts. Index data as of 25 September 2026 show the IDX SMC Composite down 21.80 % YTD and IDX SMC Liquid down 16.29 % YTD, outperforming the broader IHSG which fell 27.81 % YTD. Analysts point to sector exposure and company‑specific drivers for PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), PT Darma Henwa Tbk (DEWA) and PT Sawit Sumbermas Sarana Tbk (SSMS) as examples of second‑liner stocks with growth catalysts such as increased mining production, operating‑earnings inflection and high CPO prices. Additional buy recommendations include AKRA, DSNG, SSMS and TAPG with target prices of Rp 1,800, Rp 1,760, Rp 2,000 and Rp 2,050 respectively. Risks noted are high interest rates, rupiah and oil volatility, foreign outflows and execution risk.

articles.title: PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) reports net profit of US$54 million in H1 2026, up 830% YoY
articles.body: The issuer PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) posted net profit of US$54 million in the first half of 2026, an 830% increase from the same period in 2025. Revenue rose 67% to US$1.05 billion and EBITDA climbed 306% to US$311 million, driven by higher nickel ore production (15.2 million wet metric tonnes, up 121%) and sales (12.4 million wet metric tonnes, up 60%), as well as growth in Nickel Pig Iron and High‑Grade Nickel Matte output. The company attributed the performance to expanded mining volume, improved processing, and a new pricing formula for nickel ore, while noting ongoing ramp‑up of related assets such as PT Merdeka Tsingshan Indonesia’s acid operations, PT ESG New Energy Material’s MHP production, and the commissioning of PT Sulawesi Nickel Cobalt.

articles.title: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) posts H1 2026 net profit of US$102 million
articles.body: PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) posted a net profit attributable to owners of the parent of US$102 million for the first half of 2026, reversing a US$16 million loss a year earlier, as nickel and gold businesses strengthened. Consolidated revenue grew 64% year‑on‑year to US$1.40 billion and EBITDA surged 191% to US$512 million. The nickel segment, operating through PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA), lifted production 121% to 15.2 million wet metric tonnes and sales 60% to 12.4 million wmt, while gold output rose 32% to 66,814 ounces, driven by Tambang Emas Tujuh Bukit and the newly commissioned Tambang Emas Pani. PT ESG New Energy Material expanded Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate output and PT Sulawesi Nickel Cobalt progressed its High Pressure Acid Leach project, as MDKA pursues further growth projects and monitors commodity prices, energy costs, exchange rates and regulatory developments.

articles.title: Bank Central Asia (PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA)) stock again draws investor focus
articles.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) saw a foreign net buy of Rp 103.17 billion on 25 September 2026, lifting the share price 0.40% to Rp 6,250 with a volume of 89.45 million shares. UOB Kay Hian Sekuritas maintained a buy rating, setting a target price of Rp 8,150 (≈30% upside) and citing solid funding, capital and liquidity, while reporting August 2026 net profit of Rp 4.92 trillion (+13.1% YoY) and forecasting 2026‑2027 profits of Rp 60 trillion and Rp 65 trillion with dividend yields of 5.7% and 6.1%. The bank also refuted social‑media rumors of an acquisition by Andi Syamsuddin Arsyad (Haji Isam), confirming no corporate action plans.

articles.title: BEI removes Rp 50 floor price, opening trading range for PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO)
articles.body: The Indonesia Stock Exchange will eliminate the Rp 50 minimum price floor for all listed securities, effective 28 September 2026, directly affecting PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) which has been stuck at that level since 5 May 2026. The sell‑order queue at the Rp 50 price reached 394,120,672 lots, valued at roughly Rp 1.97 trillion as of 25 September 2026. MNC Sekuritas analyst Christian noted that the removal may allow GOTO’s price to fall below Rp 50 in the short term but should reduce trading barriers and improve liquidity and price discovery. BEI Director‑General Jeffrey Hendrik said the change is expected to boost liquidity and provide better price discovery for previously stagnant stocks such as GOTO.

articles.title: Popular news roundup highlights PT Pioneerindo Gourmet International Tbk (PTSP) CFC revenue growth, PT Pukul Rata Kanan tender for PT Guna Timur Raya Tbk (TRUK), PT Energi Mega Persada Tbk (ENRG) rights issue and PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) strong August performance
articles.body: The article presents the most popular financial news items of the week, covering performance and corporate actions of several Indonesian listed companies. PT Pioneerindo Gourmet International Tbk (PTSP) reported net revenue of Rp 385.83 billion for the first half of 2026, up from Rp 368.81 billion a year earlier, with CFC franchise sales reaching Rp 361 billion versus Rp 343.08 billion previously. PT Pukul Rata Kanan announced a voluntary tender offer for 65,250,000 shares (15 %) of PT Guna Timur Raya Tbk (TRUK) at Rp 740 per share, potentially valuing the transaction at up to Rp 48,285 billion, well below TRUK’s market price of Rp 2,580 per share on 25 September 2026. PT Energi Mega Persada Tbk (ENRG) launched a rights issue of 13,282,271,875 new B‑series shares at Rp 310 each, and PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) saw its net interest margin rise to 5.7 % in August 2026, supporting a buy recommendation with a target upside of about 30 %. The piece also notes the growing relevance of the JOMO mindset versus FOMO in investment decisions.

articles.title: BBCA and AMRT lead foreign net buying as IHSG falls on Friday (25/6/2026)
articles.body: The article reports that PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) and PT Sumber Alfaria Trijaya Tbk (AMRT) were the top stocks bought by foreign investors on a day when the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) declined. IHSG closed down 0.9% at 6,241.89 points, a 56‑point drop, marking a 3.09% weekly correction, while foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 559.07 billion on the day and Rp 4.39 trillion over the week. These net buying figures show that foreign demand concentrated on these companies despite the broader market’s selling pressure.

articles.title: Foreign investors ramp up net selling, surpassing Rp 100 trillion
articles.body: The article reports that foreign investors' net selling on the Indonesia Stock Exchange has exceeded Rp 100 trillion year‑to‑date, reaching Rp 104.3 trillion in the regular market. The biggest outflow was on PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) with a net sell of Rp 531.9 billion, followed by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) at Rp 141.1 billion, while PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) recorded the largest net buy of Rp 24.4 billion. On Thursday 24 September 2026 the composite index (IHSG) closed down 76.3 points (‑1.2%) at 6,298.6, with total market turnover of Rp 11.2 trillion, as higher U.S. Treasury yields (10‑year >5%, 2‑year ≈4.9%) and a stronger dollar pressured Indonesian assets.

articles.title: UOB Kay Hian recommends buy on PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) and hold on PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) amid tighter funding conditions
articles.body: UOB Kay Hian’s research notes that Indonesian banks are tightening funding strategies as liquidity remains constrained, and the broker maintains a buy rating on PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) while assigning hold to PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI). BBCA’s credit portfolio expanded 10.5% year‑on‑year to August 2026 with CASA growth of 10.8% YoY and a loan‑to‑deposit ratio of 81%, while BMRI’s credit grew 17.6% YoY, CASA rose 8.2% YoY and LDR reached 94.4% (potentially 101% excluding government SAL funds). BMRI relies heavily on non‑DPK funding, holding Rp 341 trillion in repo, interbank loans and securities (about 21% of its credit), compared with BBCA’s Rp 28 trillion (3% of credit), and Tier 1 capital ratios fell to 20.4% for BBRI (down 199 bps), 16.4% for BMRI (down 180 bps) and 15.5% for BBNI (down 270 bps) in the first half of 2026. The analyst notes that dividend payout ratios may be trimmed for BBRI and kept around 65% for BBNI in 2026, and that the banking sector remains cheap but UOB Kay Hian will monitor funding strength and capital adequacy before adjusting its stance.

articles.title: IHSG falls 1.20% to 6,298.61; analysts see support test at 6,200‑6,254 on Friday
articles.body: The Indonesia Stock Exchange Composite Index (IHSG) closed down 1.20% at 6,298.61 on Thursday amid foreign‑investor selling of about Rp 987 billion, higher oil prices and rising US Treasury yields. Analysts highlighted support levels at 6,254 and 6,146 and resistance at 6,352 and 6,429, while also noting a potential test of the 6,186‑6,200 range with support at 6,200 and resistance at 6,400 on Friday. The index traded below its 5‑day and 100‑day moving averages, with MACD in negative territory and Stochastic RSI in oversold condition. The sell‑off targeted major bank stocks BMRI, BBRI and telecommunications firm TLKM, which were among the shares hit by foreign investors.

articles.title: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) reports operational recovery in Q2 2026 with higher nickel ore sales and matte production, prompting a new target price
articles.body: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO), Indonesia’s largest nickel miner, is showing a gradual operational recovery in the second quarter of 2026, leading analysts to set a new target price for its shares. Nickel ore sales at the Bahodopi mine rose 21.3% quarter‑on‑quarter to 1.1 million wet metric tons, while sales from Pomalaa jumped to 496,000 wmt, almost four times the previous quarter. Nickel matte output increased 18.8% QoQ to 16.2 thousand tonnes, and the broker forecasts total matte production of 67.6 kt in 2026 and 71.0 kt in 2027. The implementation of the Harga Patokan Mineral (HPM) 363 policy is expected to boost INCO’s 2027 net profit by US$46 million, a 14.5% uplift, supported by integrated infrastructure and captive hydropower capacity of 365 MW.

articles.title: Seven Indonesian banks report the highest net profits for the first half of 2026.
articles.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) posted a net profit of Rp31.18 trillion, up 17.5% YoY; PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) earned Rp30.41 trillion, up 24.4% YoY; PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) recorded Rp29.54 trillion, up 1.8% YoY; PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk posted Rp10.80 trillion, up 6.33% YoY; Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) reported Rp4.15 trillion, up 11.08% YoY; CIMB Niaga posted Rp3.43 trillion, down 2.2% YoY; and OCBC Indonesia posted Rp2.73 trillion, up 6.39% YoY. Credit disbursements expanded across the banks, with BRI reaching Rp1,580.42 trillion (UMKM 75.1% of the portfolio), Mandiri expanding to Rp1,592 trillion, BCA’s CASA reaching Rp1,082 trillion (84.3% of DPK) and credit of Rp1,036 trillion, BNI’s credit rising to Rp968.53 trillion, and CIMB Niaga’s credit growing 12.13% to Rp193.19 trillion, while BNI’s NPL stood at 1.9% and Mandiri’s at 0.98%. The strong earnings occurred in a macro environment of 5.3% GDP growth and 3.34% inflation. CIMB Niaga’s profit decline reflected pressure on interest margins despite a 25% rise in non‑interest income and an 87.22% jump in other income, whereas OCBC Indonesia’s results were supported by integration with the OCBC Group and growth in intermediation and cheap funding.

articles.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) forecast to jump 38% and profit to soar 322%
articles.body: In a research note dated 24 September 2026, Phintraco Sekuritas projects that PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) shares could rise about 38% and its net profit could surge roughly 322% by the end of 2026. The company reported Q2‑2026 revenue of US$746 million, up 11.7% quarter‑on‑quarter, and first‑half 2026 revenue of US$1.41 billion, 23.4% higher year‑on‑year. EBITDA increased 28.4% to US$455 million, while net profit jumped 208% to US$208 million, aided by a US$70.7 million (110.9% rise) contribution from associate PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN). Oil‑and‑gas output reached 170.1 mbopd, 19% above the prior period and above the FY26 guidance of 165‑170 mbopd, driven by a 24% increase in participation rights in Block Corridor and new production from the Forel and Terubuk projects.

articles.title: Choosing Stocks with the Highest Interim Dividends for 2026 – Full List
articles.body: The article presents a list of Indonesian issuers that have announced interim dividends for the first half of 2026, highlighting those with the most generous payouts. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) will distribute an interim dividend of Rp3.07 triliun, representing 10% of its semester‑I net profit of Rp29.5 triliun, and analysts set a target price of Rp8,075. PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (CDIA) announced an interim payout ratio of 58%, while Emiten Prajogo Pangestu disclosed a dividend of US$10 juta (approximately Rp1.42 per saham). Other issuers noted for attractive interim yields include BMRI, CMRY, BSSR (with a payout around 95%) and BPII (with a payout about 82% despite a 53% YoY profit decline). Analysts caution that high interim payouts may strain cash flow for capital‑intensive firms, recommending investors consider sustainability of earnings and cash generation alongside dividend yields.

articles.title: Maybank Sekuritas sees 27.1% credit growth and maintains a buy rating for PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI)
articles.body: PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) posted a 27.1% year‑on‑year increase in credit to Rp 977 trillion in August 2026, the strongest growth among banks. Maybank Sekuritas Indonesia keeps a buy recommendation with a target price of Rp 4,800 per share, based on a projected 2026 price‑to‑book ratio of 1.0× and a current valuation of 0.8× P/BV. Net profit rose to Rp 14.3 trillion (up 6.9% YoY) supported by a 14.3% rise in net interest income, while net interest margin fell to 3.1% and provisions climbed 26.9% YoY, highlighting margin pressure and higher funding costs. Deposits grew 29.4% YoY to Rp 1,125 trillion, improving the loan‑to‑deposit ratio to 86.9% but reducing the CASA share to 65.3%, indicating a shift toward more expensive funding sources.

articles.title: Bank Indonesia Holds BI Rate at 5.75% and Panin Sekuritas Lists PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI), and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) as Top Buy Picks.
articles.body: On 23 September 2026 the Rapat Dewan Gubernur Bank Indonesia kept the BI Rate at 5.75% with the deposit facility at 4.75% and the lending facility at 6.5%. The spread between the BI Rate and the U.S. Fed rate narrowed to 1.75% from 2% and August bank credit growth rose 13.65% year‑on‑year, supporting a positive outlook for interest‑rate‑sensitive stocks. Panin Sekuritas highlighted PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) as its top buy recommendations, assigning 12‑month target prices of Rp3,856, Rp8,157, Rp5,221 and Rp4,384 respectively. Analyst consensus shows strong buying interest, with 23 analysts recommending BBRI, 35 for BBCA, 29 for BMRI and 24 for BBNI, reflecting expectations of continued credit expansion and a stable rupiah.

articles.title: ADRO, MEDC, and ARKO Compete for Green Power Export to Singapore
articles.body: The three issuers PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO), PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) and PT Arkora Hydro Tbk (ARKO) are competing to become Singapore’s green electricity supplier from the Batam‑Bintan islands. ADRO, through its subsidiary Adaro Solar International, has secured a 0.4 GW allocation from the Singapore regulator and plans a US$3.2 billion capital expenditure for the project. MEDC, via the Pacific Medco Solar Energy consortium with Grup Salim, obtained conditional approval for 600 MW within a 2 GWp Batam solar PV project. ARKO’s subsidiary Endorshine Energy Solutions received US$9.8 million financing from PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur for a commercial PLTS project, positioning ARKO as a potential dark‑horse contender.

articles.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) Facilitates 5,000 Halal Certifications for UMKM and Posts 13% YoY Net Profit Growth in August 2026
articles.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) is facilitating roughly 5,000 halal certifications for micro, small and medium enterprises (UMKM) through its Workshop Sertifikasi Halal program that began in 2023. The initiative, which includes business model canvas training, aims to boost UMKM competitiveness and has coincided with an average 8.5% revenue increase for certified UMKM according to Ministry data. In August 2026, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) reported net profit of Rp4.9 trillion, up 13% year‑on‑year and down 3% month‑to‑month, while net profit for the first eight months reached Rp40.2 trillion, 3% higher YoY and representing 67% of consensus estimates. Net interest income grew 8% YoY, credit expanded 2% month‑to‑month to Rp1,018 trillion (11% YoY) and credit cost stayed at 0.3%, below the 0.4‑0.5% guidance for 2026.

articles.title: Two PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) executives, Prijono Sugiarto and Rudy, make insider purchases, with Rudy acquiring about Rp21.14 billion of ASII shares
articles.body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) disclosed that two senior executives increased their shareholdings through direct market purchases. Komisaris Utama Prijono Sugiarto bought 8,700 shares at Rp4,850 each on 21 September 2026, spending about Rp42.19 million and raising his stake from 5,587,100 to 5,595,800 shares (0,0138% of the company). Director Rudy accumulated 4.4 million shares in two stages—2.2 million at Rp4,820 on 21 September and another 2.2 million at Rp4,790 on 22 September—totaling roughly Rp21.14 billion. His holding grew from 1.2 million to 5.6 million shares, also representing about 0,0138% of voting rights, marking a significant insider stake increase.

articles.body: BNI Sekuritas' head of retail research, Fanny Suherman, expects the Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) to face another correction on 24 Sept, with support around 6,320‑6,340 and resistance near 6,420‑6,440 after the index closed up 1.56% at 6,374.91 on 23 Sept amid a net foreign sell of Rp 468 billion. articles.title: Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BBRI) announces limited review and upcoming publication of its Q3‑2026 financial statements
articles.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) disclosed that its consolidated financial statements for the period ending 30 September 2026 will undergo a limited review by a public accountant and will be published in accordance with applicable regulations. In the first half of 2026, BRI and its subsidiaries reported a net profit of Rp30.86 trillion, up 17.42 % YoY, driven by a 5.42 % increase in interest income to Rp107.92 trillion and a 5.87 % decline in interest expense to Rp27.39 trillion, yielding net interest income of Rp80.53 trillion (+9.91 %) while impairment provisions rose 9.64 % to Rp25.51 trillion. Profitability ratios improved, with pre‑tax ROA at 3.30 %, after‑tax ROA at 2.70 % and ROE at 22.59 %, although the net interest margin fell to 6.40 % from 6.58 %, reflecting broader banking‑sector margin pressures.

articles.title: PT Elang Mahkota Teknologi Tbk (EMTK) strengthens its position in PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (BUKA) and PT Nitrasanata Dharma Tbk (JECX)
articles.body: The BEI disclosed on 22 Sep that PT Elang Mahkota Teknologi Tbk (EMTK) increased its holdings in PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (BUKA) by 188.70 million shares, raising its stake to 10.67%, and added 1.17 million shares of PT Nitrasanata Dharma Tbk (JECX) through its health subsidiary PT Sarana Meditama Metropolitan Tbk (SAME), bringing its total shareholdings to 33%. PT Yulie Sekuritas Indonesia Tbk (YULE) raised its stake in PT Esa Medika Mandiri Tbk (EMMI) to about 10.19%; Samudra (Investment) Pte. Ltd boosted its holding in PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk (MAPI) to 30.19%; and Lo Kheng Hong increased his position in PT Intiland Development Tbk (DILD) to 7.54%. Edwin Soeryadjaya now controls 35.95% of PT Saratoga Investama Sedaya Tbk (SRTG), Ferry Sudjono holds roughly 6.02% of PT Fore Kopi Indonesia Tbk (FORE), while Dato Tahir reduced his stake in PT Maha Properti Indonesia Tbk (MPRO) to 10.46%. PT Global Mediacom Tbk (BMTR) sold 28.90 million shares of its subsidiary PT Media Nusantara Citra Tbk (MNCN), lowering its control to 38.23%, and The Bank of New York Mellon divested 6 million shares of PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM), retaining about 6.3% of the telecom firm.

Total trading volume reached 36.09 billion shares with a transaction value of Rp12.54 trillion.

The strongest sector gains were in basic materials (+3.47%), energy (+2.59%) and consumer cyclical (+2.49%).

articles.title: PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (INET) and PT Solusi Sinergi Digital Tbk (WIFI) launch a 6,870‑km submarine cable project linking Jakarta and Sorong
articles.body: The consortium led by PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (INET) and PT Solusi Sinergi Digital Tbk (WIFI) has initiated the development of the SGI Cable System, a 6,870‑km submarine cable linking Jakarta with Sorong. SGI (PT Sarana Global Indonesia), a subsidiary 60% owned by INET, will act as developer and operator, and the project targets Ready for Service by the end of 2028 after a memorandum of understanding was signed on 23 September 2026. The cable will feature 16 fiber‑pair routes delivering up to 25 Tbps capacity across 14 landing points, with a design life of 25 years; PT FiberHome Technologies Indonesia expects to deliver all required materials by September 2027, Nokia Indonesia will provide high‑capacity optical network technology, and NTT Group, through PT Integrasi Jaringan Ekosistem (Weave), will supply backbone network and capacity distribution. INET will use the capacity as a majority shareholder, while WIFI (via its Surge brand) and other consortium members will also draw capacity to support expanding broadband, data‑center, cloud and AI services across Indonesia.

articles.title: ADMR Stock Stagnates Amid Strong H1 2026 Earnings, Analysts Point to Aluminium Expansion as Needed Catalyst
articles.body: PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia Tbk (ADMR) saw its share price close at Rp 1,560 on 23 September, a modest 2.63% gain that leaves the stock essentially stagnant for the year despite solid financial results. In the first half of 2026 the company posted revenue of US$584 million, up 39.3% YoY, and net profit of US$174.2 million, up 24% YoY, with mining product sales accounting for 99.6% of revenue and no aluminium contribution yet. Analysts from Mirae Asset Sekuritas and Phintraco Sekuritas argue that the market awaits proof that ADMR’s aluminium downstream expansion, pursued through PT Kalimantan Aluminium Industry and targeted to generate revenue from H2 2026 onward with a 500,000‑ton smelter capacity, can offset coal‑related volatility. Both firms maintain buy recommendations, setting target prices of Rp 2,310 and an entry range of Rp 1,505‑1,595 respectively.

articles.title: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas issues stock recommendations for HRTA, VKTR and PGEO on Thursday, 24 September 2026
articles.body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommended three stocks—HRTA, VKTR and PGEO—for trading on Thursday, 24 September 2026. HRTA’s price rebounded from a support zone of 2,100‑2,150, broke above the 20‑day moving average of 2,230 and the 200‑day moving average of 2,260, with a MACD turning positive, and the broker sees upside to 2,360‑2,475 while the company plans a private placement of up to 460.5 million new shares (≈10% of equity) ahead of an independent shareholders meeting on 16 October 2026. VKTR recovered from a Fibonacci support range of 729‑663, moved above the 200‑day moving average of 794 and, despite a still‑negative MACD, shows a potential rise to 855‑915, and the firm signed a non‑binding term sheet with BNBR and Danantara Investment Management on 1 September to explore strategic investment in a commercial electric‑vehicle ecosystem. PGEO broke out above the neckline at 1,070, stayed above the 200‑day moving average of 1,052 and formed a cup‑and‑handle pattern with a bullish MACD crossover, giving a target of 1,113‑1,140, while the company secured US$477.8 million of international funding for three geothermal projects and reported a roughly 40 % year‑on‑year profit increase in Q1 2026.

articles.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) shares see net foreign sell offset by domestic buying, closing up 0,31%
articles.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) shares recorded a net foreign sell of Rp 187.64 miliar on 23/9/2026, while domestic investors posted a net buy of Rp 187.6 miliar. Based on data from Stockbit Sekuritas, domestic investors net bought Rp 187.6 miliar, with Stokcbit Sekuritas (Rp 30.5 miliar), CGS International Sekuritas (Rp 26.7 miliar) and BCA Sekuritas (Rp 23.8 miliar) contributing, helping the stock close up 0.31% at Rp 3,190. For semester I‑2026 the bank reported PATMI of Rp 31.2 triliun, a 17.5% yoy increase, with net interest income up 9.9%, pre‑provision operating profit up 12.8%, cost of credit improving to 3.1%, total credit rising 16.2% yoy to Rp 1,645.5 triliun (corporate credit +47.1%, commercial credit +58.1%) and the micro‑credit portfolio at Rp 714.1 triliun, while gross NPL fell to 2.90% and loan at risk (LAR) improved to 9.1%. Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia maintains a buy recommendation with a 12‑month target price of Rp 4,000, implying a P/BV of 1.8 kali versus a three‑year average of 2.06 kali, while flagging risks from prolonged NIM pressure, tighter liquidity, slower credit growth, higher cost of credit and delayed micro‑asset quality recovery.

articles.title: Foreign Investors Pull Back, Leading Stocks See Heavy Selling
articles.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 461.3 billion across the Indonesian market on Wednesday, 23 September 2026, while the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) rose 97.87 points (1.56%) to 6,374.9 at the close. In total, foreign investors sold Rp 468.2 billion in the regular market, while net buying in the negotiation and cash market amounted to Rp 6.9 billion. Overall market turnover reached Rp 12.8 trillion, with 464 stocks rising, 200 falling and 299 unchanged.

articles.body: MNC Sekuritas noted that the IHSG closed up 1.56% at 6,374.91 on 23 Sep 2026 and projected the index to test support levels 6,208-6,258 before targeting a near-term strength zone of 6,387-6,418, with support at 6,267 and 6,108 and resistance at 6,440-6,535. articles.title: CreditSights maintains Underperform rating on senior bonds of PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) amid KDMP credit risk
articles.body: CreditSights kept its Underperform view on the senior bonds of PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI), noting that the bonds trade at only 100 bps and 68 bps above US Treasury yields respectively—well below the 25‑30 bps fair‑value spread to comparable Indian bank bonds—while each bank has extended Rp 55 trillion to PT Agrinas Pangan Nusantara (Agrinas) for the government‑backed KDMP program, representing 3 % of BMRI’s gross loan book and 6 % of BBNI’s. The firm highlighted the resulting pressure on capital ratios (CET1 of 16.7 % for BMRI and 15.7 % for BBNI, with projected reductions of roughly 25 bps and 43 bps) and net interest margins (KDMP loan NIM 2.2 % versus overall NIM 4.4 % for BMRI and 3.6 % for BBNI).

articles.title: IHSG Strengthens After BI Holds Rate, Analysts Recommend BNGA, BRMS, SRTG, and INDY
articles.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) rose after Bank Indonesia kept its benchmark BI‑Rate at 5.75%, and analysts highlighted four stocks. IHSG closed at 6,374.91, up 97.87 points (1.56%), while foreign investors posted a net sell of about Rp408 billion on the day and roughly Rp102.9 trillion year‑to‑date. Analysts see resistance near 6,463 and support around 6,000‑6,035, with a potential target around 6,586 if volume confirms a breakout. The recommended issuers are PT Bank CIMB Niaga Tbk (BNGA), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), PT Saratoga Investama Sedaya Tbk (SRTG) and PT Indika Energy Tbk (INDY), chosen for stable domestic rates, gold‑price exposure, strategic‑asset exposure and commodity‑sector sentiment respectively.

articles.title: ASII shares slip below IDR5,000 as President Commissioner Prijono Sugiarto and President Director Rudy increase holdings
articles.body: President Commissioner Prijono Sugiarto and President Director Rudy of ASII increased their shareholdings as the stock fell below the IDR5,000 level. Prijono bought 8,700 shares at IDR4,850 each on 21 September 2026, spending roughly IDR42.2 million, while Rudy acquired about 4.4 million shares in two transactions on 21‑22 September 2026 at IDR4,820 and IDR4,790, investing approximately IDR21.1 billion. The combined purchases lifted their collective ownership from 0,003 % to 0,0138 % and ASII closed down 0.63 % on 23 September, marking a 30.15 % decline year‑to‑date with the price remaining under IDR5,000 after briefly touching IDR5,050 on 3 September. The buying occurs amid an IDR8 trillion share buyback program that began in July 2026 and runs through July 2027, which has yet to lift the share price.

articles.title: Foreign Net Sell Surpasses Rp 100 Trillion, Keeping PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) and PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) Under Pressure
articles.body: Foreign investors' net selling in the regular market reached Rp 102.9 trillion year‑to‑date, topping the Rp 100 trillion threshold and pressuring key stocks. On Wednesday, total foreign net sell across the market was Rp 460.7 billion, with the largest outflows in PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) at Rp 187.6 billion, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) at Rp 128.7 billion and PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) at Rp 124.6 billion. Conversely, PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) attracted a net foreign buy of Rp 106.7 billion and PT Timah Tbk (TINS) a net buy of Rp 53.7 billion, while the Indonesia Stock Exchange Composite Index (IHSG) closed up 97.8 points (1.5%) at 6,374.9 with total transaction value of Rp 12.8 trillion. Market commentator Hendra Wardana said the modest index gain reflected a positive reaction to Bank Indonesia’s decision to keep the BI Rate at 5.75% despite the continued foreign outflows.

articles.title: Stock Market Outlook After Bank Indonesia Holds Benchmark Rate at 5.75%
articles.body: Bank Indonesia kept the benchmark BI Rate at 5.75% in its 22‑23 September 2026 meeting, a decision analysts view as neutral to slightly positive for equities. The analysts note that the move was largely priced in, but external pressures from the U.S. Federal Reserve’s 3.75‑4.00% policy and the risk of a 25‑basis‑point BI hike to 6.00% by year‑end keep the market volatile. They project the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) to trade between 6,186 and 6,500 in the short term and cite target prices of Rp 3,430 for BBRI, Rp 4,500 for BMRI, Rp 6,800 for BBCA, Rp 212‑Rp 268 for BUMI, Rp 1,400‑Rp 1,900 for ENRG, and Rp 2,060‑Rp 2,280 for TPIA. The outlook remains sideways to negative in the near term unless the Fed pauses rate hikes and the rupiah stabilizes.

articles.title: Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc purchases 400 million PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) shares for Rp10.8 billion, raising its stake to 7.0299%
articles.body: Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc bought 400 million shares of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) at Rp27 per share, a transaction valued at Rp10.8 billion. The purchase increased Morgan Stanley’s holding to 80.9 billion shares, representing 7,0299% of GOTO’s outstanding shares, up from 6,9951% previously. PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) will hold an extraordinary shareholders’ meeting on 14 October 2026 to consider the withdrawal of 32.18 billion Series A treasury shares and the resignation of Vice President Director Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo. These actions reflect ongoing adjustments to GOTO’s capital structure and governance.

articles.title: Big Bank Stocks Rise Cohesively After BI-Rate Held at 5.75%
articles.body: Following Bank Indonesia's decision to keep the BI-Rate at 5.75%, the shares of Indonesia's four big banks moved higher on 23 September 2026. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) led the rally, up 1.61% to Rp 6,300, while PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) rose 0.72% to Rp 4,190, PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (BBNI) gained 0.56% to Rp 3,590, and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) increased 0.31% to Rp 3,190. Analysts from Kiwoom Sekuritas and Mirae Asset Sekuritas said the rate hold offers short‑term neutral‑positive sentiment but noted that cost‑of‑fund pressures, net interest margin dynamics, and external factors such as rupiah stability and US Treasury yields could limit further upside. Target prices were set at Rp 8,075 (BBCA), Rp 5,400 (BMRI) and Rp 4,000 (BBRI) by Kiwoom, and at Rp 7,900 (BBCA), Rp 4,720 (BMRI) and Rp 4,020 (BBNI) by Mirae Asset, while net foreign selling from 14‑18 September amounted to roughly Rp 798 billion for BBCA and Rp 443.2 billion for BMRI.

articles.title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) Tightens Investment in Non-Core Businesses
articles.body: During Astra Media Day 2026 on 23 September, PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) said it will tighten its investment strategy for businesses outside its three core segments—automotive, financial services, and mining-solution & heavy-equipment operations. The company will evaluate its wider-business portfolio based on growth prospects, capital needs and contribution to the Astra ecosystem, continuing to invest in strategically important units, seeking partners for some, and re-assessing others. Wider-business segments contributed about 10% of the group’s consolidated profit, with net profit before non-recurring items of Rp1.6 trillion in the first half of 2026, a 31% increase year-on-year, while the core segments account for roughly 90% of profit. This tighter capital-allocation discipline aligns with Astra’s new corporate roadmap that emphasizes focus, clear strategy, disciplined capital deployment and transformation commitments.

articles.title: PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia Tbk (ADMR) posts 39.3% revenue growth in H1 2026 as its share price remains constrained
articles.body: PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia Tbk (ADMR) delivered a 39.3% year‑on‑year revenue increase to US$584 million in the first half of 2026, driven by a 9% rise in metallurgical coal sales and a gross margin expansion to 47.6%, while net profit rose 24% to US$174.2 million. The shares of PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia Tbk (ADMR) were largely flat YTD, trading at Rp 1,560 after a 2.63% gain on 23 September. Through PT Kalimantan Aluminium Industry, ADMR plans to generate aluminium revenue in the second half of 2026, with the smelter ramping up toward a 500,000‑ton capacity by year‑end. Analysts view the aluminium expansion as a potential catalyst but warn of short‑term operational risks from low Barito River water and commodity price volatility.

articles.body: Morgan Stanley and Co International PLC increased its ownership of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) shares ahead of the upcoming minimum‑price change. On 18 September 2026, the investor bought 400 million ordinary shares at Rp27 per share, raising its holding from 80,539,349,984 to 80,939,349,984 shares. The purchase lifted its voting rights from 6,9951 % to 7,0299 %, a 0,0348‑percentage‑point increase. The transaction occurs as Bursa Efek Indonesia will lower the minimum trading price from Rp50 to Rp1 per share effective 28 September 2026, a rule that could affect GOTO’s share price dynamics.

articles.title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) realizes Rp17 trillion capex in H1 2026.
articles.body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) has realized about Rp17 trillion in capital expenditure (capex) for the first half of 2026, representing roughly 47.2% of its annual capex budget of Rp36 trillion. The realized capex is being used to fund PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR)’s acquisition of the gold mine PT Arafura Surya Alam. With the Rp17 trillion spend, ASII still has approximately Rp19 trillion of capex remaining for the rest of 2026, and the group’s total capex for the year is projected at Rp35.6 trillion. The three core business segments continue to contribute about 89% of Astra’s net profit and revenue, underscoring the focus of the capex allocation. On the day of the announcement, ASII shares fell 0.63% to Rp4,750, marking a 2.46% decline over five days and a 30.15% drop since the start of 2026.

articles.title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) receives approval to raise coal RKAB to 12.4 million tons
articles.body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) announced that the government approved an increase in its coal work plan and budget (RKAB) to 12.4 million tons, still below its 15‑million‑ton production capacity. The new RKAB level exceeds the 7.4‑million‑ton plan approved for the first half of 2026. UNTR reported that coal sales fell 22 % to 6,723 tons and heavy‑equipment sales dropped 21 % to 2,689 units in the January‑August 2026 period, with big‑machine sales declining to 436 units from 860 units a year earlier. The company attributed the slowdown to the limited RKAB and El Nino‑related production constraints in Central Kalimantan, projecting that coal sales will only return to optimal levels in November‑December.

articles.title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) earmarks Rp7.1 trillion for share buyback through June 2026
articles.body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), a subsidiary of Astra International, has earmarked a total of Rp7.1 trillion for share repurchases from July 2022 through 30 June 2026. The company completed a buyback of 35.5 million shares between 1 April and 30 June 2026 and will be able to repurchase up to Rp2 trillion of shares between 1 July and 30 September 2026. To date, UNTR has bought back 239 million shares worth Rp7.1 trillion, while its stock has fallen 17.46% year‑to‑date and trades in a range of Rp20,125 to Rp32,825 per share. The buyback aims to reinforce investor confidence and stabilize the share price amid market volatility.

articles.title: RKAB increases to 12.4 million tons, PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) aims to boost coal production in the second half of 2026
articles.body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) raised its coal RKAB quota from about 7.4 million tons to 12.4 million tons in August 2026, giving the company a chance to boost output in the second half of the year. UNTR plans to schedule production and sales for November–December 2026 while holding some inventory, despite weather challenges from El Nino in Central Kalimantan. Coal sales through PT Tuah Turangga Agung reached 8.37 million tons in Jan–Aug 2026, a 19.44 % YoY decline from 10.39 million tons, while gold sales from Agincourt Resources and Sumbawa Jutaraya fell 73.91 % YoY to 42 000 ounces and nickel ore sales via Stargate dropped to 1.05 million wet metric tons (711 000 limonite, 348 000 saprolite) from 1.43 million tons in 2025. Coal production for UNTR’s customers via PT Pamapersada Nusantara also slipped 2.91 % YoY to 93.4 million tons.

articles.body: Institutional investor Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc purchased 400,000,000 shares of GoTo Gojek Tokopedia at IDR 27 per share, costing IDR 10,800,000,000, raising its holding to 80,939,349,984 shares (7.030% of the company) from 80,539,349,984 shares (6.995%). articles.title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reports first‑half 2026 capex of Rp 17 trillion, driven by subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR).
articles.body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) disclosed that it has realized approximately Rp 17 trillion of capital expenditure in the first half of 2026, out of a total planned capex of Rp 35‑36 trillion for the year. The majority of the spending was incurred by its subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), primarily for the acquisition of the Arafura Surya Alam gold mine and for routine purchases of heavy equipment for its mining contractor business. Astra indicated that the remaining capex budget will be allocated in a disciplined manner to support productivity and profit growth through 2027. The company said it will continue periodic evaluations to ensure the capex contributes optimally to earnings growth.

articles.title: RKAB Dampens Heavy Equipment Sales, PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) Impacted
articles.body: RKAB, the mining work-plan and budget policy, is curbing heavy equipment purchases, hitting PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) and its subsidiary PT Pamapersada Nusantara (PAMA). UNTR's Komatsu equipment sales fell 21% to 2,689 units (big-machine sales down 49% to 436 units) in the first eight months of 2026, while PAMA’s overburden removal and coal production activity slipped 8%, though UNTR’s parts and service revenue rose 1% to about Rp5.5 trillion, offsetting some pressure.

articles.body: UNTR’s coal production capacity of 15 million tons was limited to 7.4 million tons under the government‑approved RKAB, resulting in a 22 % year‑on‑year drop in coal sales to 6,723 tons for the January‑August 2026 period. articles.title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reaffirms focus on three core businesses through 2027
articles.body: On 23 September 2026, PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reaffirmed its focus on three core businesses—automotive, financial services, and mining solutions & heavy equipment—through 2027. These three segments together generate roughly 90% of the group's profit. To deepen its automotive component capabilities, the company plans to increase its stake in PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO) via a Voluntary Tender Offer at Rp 3,600 per share, requiring about Rp 858 billion if all targeted shares are acquired. Capital spending and investments will be prioritized for the three core businesses, while the firm remains open to selective opportunities outside this focus, though no significant additional investments are expected at this time.

articles.title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) feels impact of RKAB policy on coal operations and revenue
articles.body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) said the Rencana Kerja dan Anggaran Biaya (RKAB) policy continues to pressure its mining operations through August 2026. Coal production at its subsidiary Pamapersada Nusantara (PAMA) fell 3% year‑on‑year to 96.2 million tons, overburden removal dropped 8% to 670.2 million bcm and the stripping ratio slipped to 7.2 from 7.6. Revenue for the six‑month period ended 30 June 2026 declined 15% to IDR 5.8 trillion, while PAMA’s revenue still grew and a higher nickel price and a stronger US dollar partially offset the volume weakness. UNTR, which has a coal production capacity of 15 million tons, increased its approved RKAB to 12.4 million tons in August and is cutting capex and prioritising spending to navigate the dry season in Central Kalimantan.

articles.title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reports Rp17 trillion capex in H1 2026, targeting Rp36 trillion total for the year.
articles.body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) has realized Rp17 trillion of capital expenditure in the first half of 2026, which is almost half of its planned Rp36 trillion capex for the year. The bulk of the spending was driven by its mining business, primarily through its subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), covering gold and other mineral operations. The remainder of the capex consists of routine investments such as heavy‑equipment purchases for mining contractors. Astra expects to allocate the remaining roughly Rp19 trillion in the second half of 2026 in a more disciplined manner to support future growth.

articles.title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) reports coal production and heavy equipment sales fall as RKAB approvals lag
articles.body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) said its coal production and heavy equipment sales have declined because the government has not fully approved its Rencana Kerja dan Anggaran Biaya (RKAB). The company has a total coal production capacity of 15 million tons but only 7.4 million tons of RKAB were approved in the first half of 2026, about 50% of capacity, later rising to 12.4 million tons in August. Coal sales from January to August 2026 fell 22% to 6,723 tons, while heavy equipment sales dropped 21% to 2,689 units, with big‑machine sales halving to 436 units from 860 a year earlier. The downturn is also linked to El Nino‑induced dry conditions in Central Kalimantan, and the company expects coal sales to improve in the November‑December quarter.

articles.title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reports first‑half 2026 capex realization of Rp 17 trillion, 47.2% of annual target
articles.body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) said that in the first half of 2026 it has realized about Rp 17 trillion of its planned Rp 36 trillion capex, representing roughly 47.2% of the yearly target. The bulk of the realized capex was used for the acquisition of the gold mine PT Arafura Surya Alam by PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR). The remaining portion funded routine capital spending, mainly the purchase of heavy equipment to support United Tractors’ mining contractor operations. The company indicated that the balance of the capex budget will be allocated more selectively and disciplined to sustain future business growth, with ongoing evaluation.

articles.title: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) to Hold Extraordinary General Meeting on Oct 14 2026 to Approve Capital Reduction and Director Resignation
articles.body: The technology issuer PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) announced that it will convene an Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (RUPSLB) on 14 October 2026 from 10:00 to 11:30 WIB. The meeting will consider two agenda items: a capital reduction that will cancel 32,186,417,803 treasury shares of Series A bought back between 12 June 2024 and 11 June 2025, and the resignation of Vice President Director Catherine Hindra, received on 28 August 2026. The capital reduction will amend GOTO’s articles of association and cancels a previously approved employee stock ownership program that had intended to allocate the buyback shares. Shareholders recorded on the shareholder list as of 21 September 2026, or holding shares in accounts at PT Kustodian Sentral Efek Indonesia (KSEI) at the close of trading on that date, are eligible to attend.

articles.title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) posts 21.09% YoY drop in Komatsu equipment sales and sharp declines in gold and nickel output in August 2026
articles.body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) recorded a 21.09% year‑on‑year decline in Komatsu heavy‑equipment sales, delivering 2,689 units in the January‑August 2026 period versus 3,408 units a year earlier. Mining accounted for 52% of those sales, while August alone saw 296 units sold, a 32.58% month‑on‑month drop from July’s 399 units. Overburden removal through PT Pamapersada Nusantara fell 8.46% YoY to 670.2 million bcm and coal sales via PT Tuah Turangga Agung slipped 19.44% YoY to 8.37 million tons, while gold sales from Agincourt Resources and Sumbawa Jutaraya fell 73.91% YoY to 42,000 ounces and nickel ore sales via Stargate declined to 1.05 million wet metric tons. The data, reported on 23 September, highlights weakening demand across UNTR’s mining‑related equipment and mineral‑product segments.

articles.title: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) seeks shareholder approval to cancel 32.18 billion treasury shares, with buyback program continuing
articles.body: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) is requesting shareholder approval at an extraordinary general meeting on 14 October 2026 to cancel approximately 32.18 billion treasury shares, representing 80.89% of its total treasury holdings of 39.78 billion shares. The treasury shares were acquired through a buyback program from 12 June 2024 to 11 June 2025 that cost Rp2.09 trillion, and the company plans to eliminate them via a capital reduction rather than the previously intended ESOP/MSOP allocation. PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) also announced that a further buyback of up to Rp3.5 trillion will be carried out from 19 June 2026 to 18 June 2027, funded from internal resources and not from public offerings or debt. The cancellation is expected to increase earnings per share, and the meeting will also consider the resignation of Vice President Director Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo.

articles.title: CreditSights: Village Co‑op Loan Program Pressures Profitability of Bank Mandiri and Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI)
articles.body: CreditSights finds the Village Co‑op Loan Program (KDMP) is likely to pressure the profitability of Bank Mandiri and Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI), the state‑owned banks ('perbankan BUMN') involved. Both banks have each extended about Rp55 trillion to PT Agrinas Pangan Nusantara, representing roughly 3 % of Bank Mandiri’s and 6 % of BNI’s gross loan portfolios, and the KDMP loan carries a net interest margin of about 1.4 % versus 4.4 % for Bank Mandiri and 3.6 % for BNI in Q2‑2026. The KDMP loan’s return on assets is estimated at 0.7 % compared with 2.1 % for Bank Mandiri and 1.4 % for BNI, making the loan dilutive to both banks’ margins and ROA. CreditSights notes that while direct credit‑risk is low due to government repayment mechanisms, the low‑yield lending could slow credit‑growth to low‑teens in H2‑2026 and pressure earnings despite strong capital positions.

articles.title: PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) invests US$200 million for 37% of Zankore, target price lifted to Rp4,650
articles.body: PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) has injected US$200 million of internal cash to acquire a 37% equity stake in Zankore, valuing the AI‑computing venture at a post‑money equity of US$540 million. Indo Premier Sekuritas estimates the first 100 MW Zankore project, slated to start operations in the second half of 2027, could generate US$1.3 billion of revenue, US$158 million of net profit and, based on Indosat’s 37% share, contribute roughly US$58 million to ISAT’s net earnings annually. The brokerage also highlights Infra Fiber Teknologi (IFT), a subsidiary of Indosat, which posted revenue of Rp2.4 trillion and EBITDA of Rp1.85 trillion and is expected to add Rp279‑281 billion to ISAT’s core net profit each year through fiber expansion and AI‑related GPU rack operations. Accordingly, Indo Premier raises its 2027‑2028 core net‑profit forecast for ISAT by 4%‑17%, switches to a sum‑of‑the‑parts valuation and lifts its target price to Rp4,650 per share, while the stock trades around Rp2,380, down 1.24%.

articles.title: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) posts strong H1 2026 earnings and receives buy ratings with target prices near IDR 4,000
articles.body: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) delivered solid first‑half 2026 results, posting net profit of Rp 31.18 trillion, up 17.5% YoY, and credit disbursements rising 16.2% YoY with corporate and commercial loan growth of 47.1% and 58.1% respectively. Asset quality improved as the gross non‑performing loan ratio fell to 2.9% from 3.1% and the risk‑weighted asset ratio (LAR) declined to 9.1% from 10.8%. Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia and Maybank Sekuritas Indonesia each issued buy recommendations, setting 12‑month target prices of IDR 4,000 and IDR 3,900 respectively, implying upside of roughly 26% and 22% from the recent closing price of IDR 3,180. Bloomberg’s consensus of 33 analysts also favours a buy stance, with a median target price of IDR 3,856.83 and an implied upside of more than 21%, while management projects credit growth of 8‑10% and a net interest margin of 7.4‑7.8% for 2026.

articles.title: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommends BIPI, RMKE and CUAN for trading on 23 September 2026
articles.body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas issued a broker recommendation for three stocks—BIPI, RMKE and CUAN—on Wednesday, 23 September 2026. BIPI’s share price has rebounded above its 20‑day moving average (MA20) of 146 after breaking support at 131‑138, and the company reported a net profit of Rp 76.4 billion in Q2‑2026, reversing a loss of Rp 160.7 billion in the same quarter a year earlier. RMKE is trading above the 400‑388 support zone but below its MA20 of 416, while the firm posted H1‑2026 revenue of Rp 1.6 trillion (+176.7 % YoY) and net profit of Rp 163.3 billion (+89.6 % YoY), driven by higher coal and logistics volumes. CUAN remains above its MA20 of 906 and the 855‑914 support range, and is negotiating to acquire control of SINI, already holding 27.78 % of SINI shares through PT Kreasi Jasa Persada and PT Petrosea (PTRO).

articles.body: BNI Sekuritas' Head of Retail, Fanny Suherman, forecasts a short-term technical rebound for Indonesia's composite index (IHSG) to the 6,300-6,320 range, noting support at 6,200-6,220 and resistance at 6,300-6,320, and warning that failure to break above 6,320 may lead to a correction toward 5,850-6,100, after the index closed at 6,277.04 on 22 September 2026. It also advises PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (MDKA) – speculative buy at Rp 2,800‑Rp 2,830, target Rp 2,870‑Rp 2,940; PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (INET) – buy on weakness at Rp 304‑Rp 316, target Rp 320‑Rp 330; and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (ADRO) – buy on weakness at Rp 2,580‑Rp 2,610, target Rp 2,630‑Rp 2,680.

articles.title: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) shares fall despite higher production quota
articles.body: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) shares closed at Rp25,300 on 22 September 2026, down 825 points or 3.16% as the broader IDX fell 1.69%. The decline came after the company received approval in August 2026 to raise its production quota to about 23 million tonnes, slightly above its 2026 target of 22‑22.9 million tonnes. In the first half of 2026, coal output fell 5% YoY to 9.9 million tonnes, while second‑quarter output rose 13% QoQ to 5.3 million tonnes, and sales increased 5% YoY to 12.3 million tonnes with the average selling price up 4% to US$81 per tonne. Revenue for H1 2026 reached roughly US$1 billion, up 9% YoY, and attributable net profit was US$106 million, while the coal reference price fell to US$123.54 per tonne. Analysts have lifted the target price to around Rp30,000 per share, citing the higher quota and improved margins, though they note limited visibility on future production growth and operational cost risks.

articles.title: Analyst highlights nickel stock recommendations and sector outlook amid RKAB and HPM regulatory pressure
articles.body: David Kurniawan of PT Indo Premier Sekuritas says nickel issuers remain under pressure in 2026 because of global oversupply, uncertainty over RKAB approval and new HPM regulations. Year‑to‑date, PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) fell 9.57%, PT Trimegah Bangun Persada Tbk (NCKL) dropped 18.67%, PT Merdeka Battery Materials Tbk (MBMA) slid 11.3%, PT Central Omega Resources Tbk (DKFT) declined 8.97%, PT PAM Mineral Tbk (NICL) plunged 64.61%, while PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) posted a modest 0.63% gain. The analyst notes that integrated issuers such as ANTM and INCO have stronger resilience due to diversified portfolios and healthy capital structures. He expects the sector’s outlook to improve gradually in 2027 if RKAB approvals proceed smoothly and cost‑efficiency measures take effect.

articles.title: Foreign investors heavily bought ten stocks as the IHSG fell 1.68% to 6,277 on Tuesday (22/9)
articles.body: Foreign investors recorded net purchases in ten Indonesian listed companies while the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.68% (107 points) to 6,277.04 on Tuesday (22/9/2026). These net purchases occurred despite the broader market correction.

articles.title: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) secures approval for its 2026 RKAB, raising the production quota to ~23 Mt and prompting buy recommendations
articles.body: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) has received government approval for its revised 2026 Work Plan and Budget (RKAB), increasing the coal production quota to roughly 23 million tonnes. In the first half of 2026 the company reported revenue of about US$1 billion, up 9% YoY, and net profit attributable to shareholders of US$106 million, up 16% YoY, while production was 9.9 million tonnes, down 5% YoY but Q2 output rose 13% QoQ to 5.3 million tonnes. UBS Sekuritas and KB Valbury Sekuritas upgraded their outlook, issuing buy recommendations with target prices of Rp 30,000 and Rp 29,300 per share respectively, whereas Mirae Asset Sekuritas advised a wait‑and‑see stance. The firm faces risks from higher mining and transport costs, logistics constraints and possible tighter quota approvals for 2027‑2028, while its renewable‑energy portfolio grew to 86 MWp of operating solar capacity, supporting its long‑term diversification strategy.

articles.title: Factors Driving PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) Net Profit Surge 796% YoY
articles.body: The article explains the drivers behind PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC)’s net profit surge of 796.52% YoY to US$275.32 million in the first half of 2026. The jump results from a 23.35% revenue increase to US$1.41 billion, a 30.17% rise in gross profit to US$588.5 million, and a US$124.11 million contribution from associate PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) (US$104.17 million), joint‑venture PT Transportasi Gas Indonesia (TGI) (US$17.16 million) and affiliated PT Api Metra Graha (AMG) (US$2.10 million), while cost of goods sold grew only 18.92% as exploration expenses fell 73.06% and electricity‑sales costs dropped 15.33%. Consequently, Medco’s net profit margin rose to 19.46% from 2.68% in H1 2025, with the sharp YoY growth also reflecting the low profit base of US$100.92 million in H1 2025 after a 72.53% decline from 2024.

articles.title: Stock Moves of Salim to Prajogo Conglomerate Issuers: Who Delivered the Highest Returns?
articles.body: The article reviews the year‑to‑date (YTD) share‑price performance of issuers affiliated with Salim Group, Astra Group and Prajogo Pangestu group in 2026. Salim affiliates PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk (LSIP) surged 36.82% to Rp1,635, reporting 16% revenue growth to Rp2.69 trillion and a 25% net‑profit rise to Rp891 billion, while PT Salim Ivomas Pratama Tbk (SIMP) and PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF) posted gains of 7.89% to Rp615 and 3.32% to Rp7,000 respectively. Astra affiliates PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO) climbed 25.28% to Rp3,370 with revenue up 13.2% to Rp10.9 trillion and net profit up 22.6% to about Rp1.15 trillion, PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) rose 13.22% to Rp8,350, and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) fell 16.27% to Rp24,700. Prajogo Pangestu affiliates PT Petrosea Tbk (PTRO) dropped 50.57% to Rp5,400 despite a 59.56% revenue jump to US$543.98 million, and PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) also slumped sharply, underscoring weaker YTD returns for the Prajogo group.

articles.title: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) targets production recovery and new stock recommendations
articles.body: PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) is expected to restore coal production toward its 2026 target and analysts have issued new stock recommendations. Production in the first half of 2026 was 9.9 million tons (‑5% YoY), while second‑quarter output rose 13% QoQ to 5.3 million tons, and the government approved a 2026 RKAB quota of about 23 million tons, slightly above the company’s target of 22‑22.9 million tons. The company’s revenue grew 9% YoY to roughly US$1 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders increased 16% YoY to US$106 million, supported by a 5% rise in sales volume and a 4% increase in average selling price; it projects 2026 revenue of US$2.08 billion and net profit of US$223 million. Analysts recommend buying ITMG with target prices of Rp 29,300 and Rp 30,000 per share, while one analyst suggests a wait‑and‑see approach.

articles.body: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) announced that its extraordinary shareholders meeting (RUPSLB) will be held on 14 October 2026 with a hybrid format and a physical attendance cap of 80 participants on a first‑come‑first‑served basis. At the close of trading on 22 September 2026, GOTO’s shares were unchanged at Rp50 per share, and the company recorded 464,713 single‑investor shareholders as of the end of August 2026.

articles.title: Rupiah weakens and IHSG falls 1.69% as PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) record the largest transaction values
articles.body: The Indonesian rupiah weakened 0.21% to IDR 17,884 per US dollar and the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.69% to 6,277.04 on Tuesday. Trading volume reached Rp14.45 trillion across 33.71 billion shares, with PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) recording the largest transaction values of Rp875.45 billion and Rp714.09 billion respectively, while BUMI’s share price fell 3.64% and also fell 4.17% as reported. All sector indices slipped, led by energy down 2.76% and consumer‑cyclical up only 0.33%, and the IHSG broke below its 100‑day and 60‑day moving averages, potentially testing the psychological 6,200 level. Analysts noted that investors await the Bank Indonesia board meeting, with consensus expecting the BI Rate to stay at 5.75%, and the IHSG was the worst‑performing emerging‑market index in the Asia‑Pacific region that day.

articles.title: Nickel stocks pressured by RKAB approval uncertainty and HPM regulation, PT PAM Mineral Tbk (NICL) leads declines.

Outlook for 2027 is cautiously optimistic, contingent on smoother RKAB licensing, cost‑efficiency gains, and potential demand recovery from electric‑vehicle batteries and stainless‑steel markets.

articles.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) posts H1 2026 net profit of US$275.31 million, up 796.6% YoY, on higher oil prices
articles.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) reported a sharp rise in first‑half 2026 profit driven by higher oil prices. Revenue grew 23.35% year‑on‑year to US$1.41 billion, with contract revenue of US$1.38 billion and financial income of US$29.27 million, while cost of goods sold rose 18.92% to US$826.25 million. Net profit reached US$275.31 million, a 796.6% YoY increase from US$30.70 million in the same period of 2025, and production averaged 170,000 mboepd, of which gas contributed about 72%. BCA Sekuritas analyst Hernanda Cahyo expects Brent oil to stay near US$100 per barrel in 2026 and cites upcoming projects such as Senoro Phase 2A, Bualuang Renewal Plan Phase I and the Sambar field as additional growth drivers, while warning of risks from geopolitics, price declines and higher operating costs.

articles.title: IHSG drops over 1% as PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI) drags the index
articles.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 84.62 points, or 1.33%, to 6,300.11 on 22 September 2026, extending the decline from the previous session. The drop was led by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), which alone pulled the index down 14.6 points, followed by PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) (-7.74 points), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS) (-2.98 points), PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM) (-2.77 points), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) (-2.45 points), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) (-2.21 points), PT Bumi Resources Tbk (BUMI) (-2.21 points), PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (DSSA) (-2.15 points), PT Impack Pratama Industri Tbk (IMPC) (-2.11 points) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) (-1.98 points). In contrast, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) added the most positive impact with +2.11 points, while PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) and PT Indosat Tbk (ISAT) contributed +0.38 and +0.36 points respectively. Broad sector weakness saw energy, utilities and property lead the red zone, and the market remained sensitive to domestic uncertainty over the upcoming Bank Indonesia rate decision and global oil price and geopolitical tensions.

articles.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) net profit soars 796% in H1 2026
articles.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC), the listed oil‑and‑gas issuer, reported net profit of US$275.31 million for the first half of 2026, a 796.60% increase year‑on‑year from US$30.70 million in the same period of 2025. Revenue rose 23.35% YoY to US$1.41 billion, driven by contract revenue of US$1.38 billion (up 23.37% YoY) and financial income of US$29.27 million (up 22.42% YoY). Cost of goods sold and direct expenses increased 18.92% YoY to US$826.25 million, while total assets grew 8.02% to US$9.03 billion and liabilities rose 8.36% to US$6.05 billion, leaving equity at US$2.52 billion as of 30 June 2026. The earnings surge underscores MEDC's strong performance in its oil‑and‑gas operations during the first half of 2026.

articles.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) records solid H1 2026 performance, net profit reaches US$275 million
articles.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) posted a net profit of US$275 million for the first half of 2026, up 796.5% from US$30.71 million in the same period of 2025. The company reported revenue of US$1,415 billion, EBITDA of US$805 million, gross profit of US$588 million, and oil‑and‑gas production of 170,000 boepd (72% gas) with a production cost of US$8.4 per boe, below its US$10 guidance. Electricity sales rose to 2,323 GWh, with renewables accounting for about 25% of sales, and Medco reaffirmed its 2026 guidance of 165,000‑170,000 boepd production, 4,550 GWh electricity sales, and capex of US$450‑475 million for oil‑and‑gas plus up to US$50 million for electricity. CEO Ronald Gunawan highlighted the full‑scale operation of Senoro Phase 2A, the on‑track progress of Sakakemang gas, and new production contracts in Indonesia, Thailand, Oman, Malaysia and the South Natuna Sea as drivers of the strong results.

articles.title: Shareholding changes above 5% on 18 Sep: Dato Tahir reduces MPRO stake to 10.49% and notable transactions in NSSS, YULE, JECX, MAPI, PRDA and UNTR
articles.body: On 18 Sep, Dato Tahir sold 37 million shares of PT Maha Properti Indonesia Tbk (MPRO), lowering his ownership from 10.86% to 10.49%. In PT Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera Tbk (NSSS), Samuel International divested 534.17 million shares (down to 12.9%), PT Samuel Sekuritas Indonesia sold 611.33 million shares (down to 14.06%), PT Nusantara Makmur Lestari cut its holding to about 9.46%, while PT Samuel Tumbuh Bersama bought 3.59 billion shares, raising its stake to 36.75%. Sabrina Evelyn Elian increased her holding in PT Yulie Sekuritas Indonesia Tbk (YULE) to 5.18%; Emtek, through PT Sarana Meditama Metropolitan Tbk (SAME), added 413 000 shares of PT Nitrasanata Dharma Tbk (JECX) to a 32.95% stake, and Samudra (Investment) Pte. Ltd. purchased 2.35 million shares of PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk (MAPI), bringing its ownership to 30.08%. The session ended with buybacks: PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (PRDA) repurchased 404 400 shares, holding 6.24% of its stock, and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) bought back 464 600 shares, holding 7.84%.

articles.title: PT Amman Mineral International Tbk (AMMN) reports first‑half 2026 net profit of US$497.92 million, reversing a US$148.72 million loss from the same period a year earlier.
articles.body: PT Amman Mineral International Tbk (AMMN) turned a net loss of US$148.72 million in the first half of 2025 into a net profit of US$497.92 million in the first half of 2026. The profit swing was driven by a 1,024 % year‑on‑year increase in sales to US$2.05 billion and a 1,207 % rise in EBITDA to US$1.13 billion, supported by an 81 % rise in concentrate production to 347,307 metric tons, a 136 % jump in copper output to 211 million pounds, and a 481 % surge in gold output to 346,354 ounces. The company also received its Smelter Project Acceptance Certificate in July 2026 and began commissioning an expansion of its concentrator plant in mid‑August 2026. Stockbit Sekuritas highlighted that a copper price averaging US$14,000 per ton and potential by‑product contributions from silver and sulfuric acid could further bolster AMMN’s second‑half performance.

articles.title: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) reports net profit up nearly 800% in H1 2026
articles.body: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) posted a net profit of US$275.32 million for the first half of 2026, a 796.5% increase from US$30.71 million a year earlier. Revenue rose 23.35% to US$1.41 billion and EBITDA reached US$805 million, while production averaged 170 k barrels of oil equivalent per day, with gas accounting for about 72% of output. Consolidated debt stood at US$4.13 billion against cash of US$1.4 billion, giving a net‑debt‑to‑EBITDA ratio of 1.4×, well below the 2.5× guidance, and electricity sales hit 2,323 GWh, with renewables contributing roughly 25% of the mix. The results were supported by full‑capacity operations at the Senoro Phase 2A smelter, contributions from PT Amman Mineral Internasional, new production sharing contracts in Indonesia and Malaysia, and the company retained its idAA‑ rating from Pefindo with unchanged international ratings.

articles.title: RKAB revision delays weigh on mining services issuers; analyst recommends UNTR
articles.body: Delays in approving revised RKAB plans until September 2026, affecting about 50 mining companies, create uncertainty for mining services issuers. Analysts note that the 2026 coal production quota is projected at about 600 million tonnes, roughly 24 % lower than 2025, which could reduce contractors' work volume and pressure margins. PT Indo Premier Sekuritas analyst Brigita Kinari and BRI Danareksa Sekuritas analyst Abida Massi Armand stress diversification across commodities and recommend buying UNTR with a target price of Rp 30,600 per share. The impact of the RKAB delay is expected to be most felt in 2027, with diversified issuers likely to recover faster.

articles.title: Foreign Investors Target Top Ten Stocks as IHSG Corrects to 6,384
articles.body: Foreign investors were net buyers of the ten most purchased stocks on Monday as the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) corrected to 6,384.72. The IHSG closed at 6,384.72, down 0.88% (56.43 points) with a low of 6,381 and a high of 6,451, total volume of 26.78 billion shares and transaction value of Rp 11.77 trillion, while foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 510.07 billion. The net‑buy amounts were: PT Timah Tbk (TINS) Rp 50.02 billion, PT Petrosea Tbk (PTRO) Rp 37.9 billion, PT Indokripto Koin Semesta Tbk (COIN) Rp 31.19 billion, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) Rp 29.42 billion, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (BBRI) Rp 23.11 billion, PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) Rp 22.72 billion, PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (TPIA) Rp 21.51 billion, PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (TAPG) Rp 20.91 billion, PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk (LSIP) Rp 16.09 billion, and PT Folago Global Nusantara Tbk (IRSX) Rp 12.69 billion. In total, 354 stocks fell, 280 rose and 156 were unchanged, making these ten stocks among the net‑buy leaders despite overall foreign net selling.
